title: App permissions
intro: A permission is when an app asks to use something on your phone: the camera, microphone, location, contacts or photos.
The big question: does the app need it to work? A camera app needs the camera. A flashlight doesn't need your contacts.
When a request looks strange, tap 'Don't allow' and ask a parent. You can always change it later in Settings.

game.prompt: Does each request make sense, or is it suspicious?

items.text: A photo app asks to use the camera
items.explain: It needs the camera to take photos. Makes sense.

items.text: A flashlight app asks for your contacts
items.explain: A flashlight just makes light. It has no reason to see your contacts.

items.text: A map app asks for your location
items.explain: To show you the way, a map needs to know where you are.

items.text: A puzzle game asks to use the microphone all the time
items.explain: A puzzle doesn't need to hear you. A request like that is a reason to stop and ask.

items.text: A drawing app asks to save your picture to your photos
items.explain: To save your picture, it needs to reach your photos. Makes sense.

items.text: A calculator asks to know where you are
items.explain: A calculator does sums. It doesn't need your location.

quiz.question: What is a permission?
options: An app asking to use something on your phone
quiz.explain: A permission is something you let an app do, like use the camera or know where you are.

quiz.question: An app asks for something it doesn't need. What do you do?
options: Allow it quickly to start playing
Tap 'Don't allow' and ask a parent
quiz.explain: You're allowed to say no. If the app really needs it, your parents can help decide.

quiz.question: You allowed a permission and changed your mind. Can you undo it?
quiz.explain: In Settings you can see and change every permission. It's a good idea to do it with a parent.

summary: Before allowing a permission, ask: does the app really need this? If the request is strange, tap 'Don't allow' and ask a parent. You can change it all later in Settings.
